blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (The provider call has no timeout) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (Unbounded retry of a non-idempotent charge can duplicate charges) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Pass an explicit `timeout=` (connect and read) to `requests.post`. Without it, when the payment provider accepts the connection but stops answering, `charge()` blocks forever on the checkout path: the request worker hangs, nothing is logged and the operator only sees checkouts piling up.
findings.title: The provider call has no timeout

findings.recommendation: Bound the retries (a few attempts, exponential backoff with jitter), then raise an error naming the order. Retry only when the charge is safe to repeat: send an idempotency key derived from `order_id` that the provider honours, and do not retry on 4xx responses. Today, when the provider charges the card but the response is lost (read error, 5xx after processing), the loop posts the charge again every second and charges the customer twice; when the provider is down or rejects the request (e.g. a 400 for an invalid amount), the loop never ends and hammers the provider at 1 request per second per pending order.
findings.title: Unbounded retry of a non-idempotent charge can duplicate charges

findings.recommendation: Log each failed attempt as a structured event (order id, attempt number, HTTP status, error class, no request body or credentials) and emit a metric for charge failures. Today, when the provider returns errors, the exception is dropped: an operator investigating a stuck checkout has no log, no status code and no order id to diagnose from.
findings.title: Failed charge attempts are swallowed without a log

findings.recommendation: Read the provider URL from the environment or configuration (e.g. `PAYMENT_URL` env var), with no production default for non-production environments. The task is verified against the provider's sandbox, yet the code only knows the production endpoint: pointing a test or staging environment at the sandbox needs a code edit, and an environment run as is sends real charges to production.
findings.title: Provider URL is hard-coded
